Codon and amino acid consequence of each SNV

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/annotate-codon.R
annotateCodonChange.Rd

Annotates every single-nucleotide substitution in a WithinHostExperiment with the codon it changes and the resulting amino acid, by passing the sites to VariantAnnotation::predictCoding(). The coding sequences are supplied either as a TxDb or as the CDS records of an annotation in a GRanges or GRangesList; the reference sequence is a DNAStringSet, as returned by Biostrings::readDNAStringSet().

Usage

annotateCodonChange(x, cds, ref, ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,TxDb,DNAStringSet'
annotateCodonChange(x, cds, ref, collapse = c("longest", "all"), ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,GRangesList,DNAStringSet'
annotateCodonChange(
  x,
  cds,
  ref,
  geneCol = NULL,
  collapse = c("longest", "all"),
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,GRanges,DNAStringSet'
annotateCodonChange(
  x,
  cds,
  ref,
  txCol = "ID",
  geneCol = "gene",
  collapse = c("longest", "all"),
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,ANY,character'
annotateCodonChange(x, cds, ref, ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,ANY,XString'
annotateCodonChange(x, cds, ref, ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,character,DNAStringSet'
annotateCodonChange(x, cds, ref, ...)

Arguments

x

A WithinHostExperiment with ref and alt columns in mcols(rowRanges(x)).

cds

The coding sequences: a TxDb; a GRanges of CDS records; or a GRangesList with one element per transcript, holding its CDS parts.

ref

A DNAStringSet with the reference sequence of each seqlevel carrying coding sequences, for example from Biostrings::readDNAStringSet().

...

Not used; supplying anything is an error.

collapse

Either "longest" (default) or "all"; see Details.

geneCol

The column of gene labels reported as GENEID. For a GRanges it is a column of the CDS records, mcols(cds), defaulting to "gene"; for a GRangesList it is a column of the list's own metadata, one value per transcript, defaulting to NULL. NULL reports the transcript name instead of a gene label.

txCol

For a GRanges cds: the column identifying the transcript each CDS record belongs to (default "ID").

Value

x, with these columns added to mcols(rowRanges(x)) (NA, or an empty element, for sites not annotated):

TXNAME

Transcript the row describes.

GENEID

Gene of that transcript.

CONSEQUENCE

"synonymous", "nonsynonymous" or "nonsense"; see Details. A site whose reference codon holds an ambiguous base is NA in every column.

CDSLOC

Position of the site within the coding sequence.

PROTEINLOC

Position of the affected codon in the protein.

REFCODON, VARCODON

Reference and variant codon, on the transcript's strand.

REFAA, VARAA

Reference and variant amino acid, "*" for a stop codon.

Details

Coding sequences. predictCoding() reads coding sequences from a TxDb. A GRanges of CDS records, for example the rows of rtracklayer::import() with type == "CDS", is grouped into transcripts by the column txCol: in GFF3 files from NCBI and Ensembl the CDS records of one protein share an ID. Each transcript's parts are joined in order of transcription, so a CDS split across a ribosomal frameshift, such as SARS-CoV-2 ORF1ab, is translated as one sequence. The TxDb is then built with txdbmaker::makeTxDb(), which is why that route needs the txdbmaker package.

Building a TxDb directly from a GFF3 file with txdbmaker::makeTxDbFromGFF() is not equivalent for every annotation. For the NCBI SARS-CoV-2 annotation (NC_045512.2) it drops the ORF1ab gene, whose two CDS parts overlap by one nucleotide, with a warning that its exon ranks could not be inferred; sites in ORF1a and ORF1ab are then left unannotated. A TxDb gives no record of what was dropped while it was built, so this function cannot detect it. Pass the CDS records as a GRanges when in doubt.

A GFF3 phase column, when present, is honoured: the first part of each transcript is shortened by its phase, the number of bases before the first complete codon, and the phase of every later part must agree with the length of the parts before it. A later part whose phase disagrees would shift the reading frame of the joined sequence, so the function stops.

Reference. Sequence names in ref are cut at the first space, so a FASTA header carrying a description still matches the annotation. The function stops if the variant sites and the coding sequences share no sequence name (see annotateGenes), or if a sequence carrying coding sequences is missing from ref. Sites whose ref allele differs from the reference base at that position are left unannotated, with a warning, since they were called against a different sequence. The length of each reference sequence is recorded in seqlengths(rowRanges(x)).

Sites annotated. Only single-nucleotide substitutions with alleles A, C, G or T are annotated; insertions, deletions and multi-nucleotide substitutions get NA. Alleles are read on the plus strand and complemented by predictCoding() for transcripts on the minus strand.

Classification. CONSEQUENCE is taken from predictCoding() unchanged: "synonymous" when the amino acid is kept, "nonsense" when a stop codon is gained, and "nonsynonymous" for every other change, including the loss of a stop codon. A codon holding an ambiguous base is not translated; such a site is left unannotated, with a warning.

predictCoding() applies the initiator rule of Biostrings::translate() only when the substitution is the first base of a coding sequence: there an alternative start codon (CTG or TTG) is reported as M, so ATG to CTG at that one position is synonymous. A change at the second or third base of the first codon is translated with the standard table, giving L for CTG.

Sites in several transcripts. predictCoding() returns one row per site and transcript, so a site where coding sequences overlap (ORF1a and ORF1ab in SARS-CoV-2) has several. With collapse = "longest" (the default) the row of the transcript with the longest coding sequence is kept, ties going to the transcript that appears first in cds, and a message reports how many sites had more than one transcript and at how many of them the consequence differed between transcripts. With collapse = "all" every row is kept: each column becomes a CharacterList or IntegerList with one element per transcript.

A nucleotide that one transcript reads twice, the nucleotide shared by the two parts of a CDS split across a -1 ribosomal frameshift (SARS-CoV-2 ORF1ab at 13468), gives that transcript two rows, one for each reading. With collapse = "longest" the first reading, at the lower CDS position, is kept, and a message says how many sites this affected and at how many the two readings differ in consequence; collapse = "all" keeps both. pNpSWithinHost counts such a site by the first of its readings in a sense codon.

References

Obenchain V, Lawrence M, Carey V, Gogarten S, Shannon P, Morgan M (2014). VariantAnnotation: a Bioconductor package for exploration and annotation of genetic variants. Bioinformatics 30:2076-2078. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btu168

See also

annotateGenes for gene labels without codons; VariantAnnotation::predictCoding().

Examples

## A 15-nucleotide coding sequence, ATG CTG AAA GGG TAA
ref <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(c(seg1 = "ATGCTGAAAGGGTAA"))
cds <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("seg1", IRanges::IRanges(1, 15),
    strand = "+", ID = "cds-A", gene = "geneA")
gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("seg1",
    IRanges::IRanges(c(1, 6, 13), width = 1))
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$ref <- c("A", "G", "T")
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$alt <- c("G", "A", "C")
whe <- WithinHostExperiment(
    assays = list(altFreq = matrix(c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3), ncol = 1)),
    rowRanges = gr,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_id = "S1"))
if (requireNamespace("txdbmaker", quietly = TRUE)) {
    whe <- annotateCodonChange(whe, cds, ref)
    mc <- S4Vectors::mcols(SummarizedExperiment::rowRanges(whe))
    mc[, c("GENEID", "REFCODON", "VARCODON", "REFAA", "VARAA",
           "CONSEQUENCE")]
}
#> DataFrame with 3 rows and 6 columns
#>        GENEID    REFCODON    VARCODON       REFAA       VARAA   CONSEQUENCE
#>   <character> <character> <character> <character> <character>   <character>
#> 1       geneA         ATG         GTG           M           V nonsynonymous
#> 2       geneA         CTG         CTA           L           L    synonymous
#> 3       geneA         TAA         CAA           *           Q nonsynonymous
